entrada-biblia-01.context: The Bible brings together many books, written over centuries, but it tells a single story. It does not begin with a hero, a people, or a king. These first verses set the stage where everything that follows will happen.
entrada-biblia-01.focusQuestion: What difference does it make to read your life within a story that begins in God?
entrada-biblia-01.keywordGloss: The beginning of everything; the Bible opens its story with God already present and at work.
facts: The Bible begins with God creating the heavens and the earth.
Before the light, there was darkness over the face of the deep.
God speaks, and light comes into being.
God sees that the light is good and separates it from the darkness.
God names the light and the darkness: Day and Night.
The text marks evening and morning and counts the first day.

entrada-biblia-02.context: In Genesis 2, God gave human beings a whole garden and a single prohibition: not to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. Now the serpent enters the scene. It does not use force: it uses questions and half-truths about what God said.
entrada-biblia-02.focusQuestion: In what area of your life have you been hearing the question "Did God really say that?"
entrada-biblia-02.keywordGloss: Doubting God's word and goodness; in the text, it is the step that comes before the fruit.
facts: The serpent was craftier than all the wild animals.
The serpent begins with a question about what God said.
The woman answers that they may eat the fruit of the trees in the garden.
The serpent claims they will not die.
The woman ate the fruit and also gave some to her husband, who ate.

entrada-biblia-03.context: After the fall, the story only grows darker: Cain kills his brother, the flood comes, and at Babel the peoples are scattered. In Genesis 12, the Lord speaks to a man living in Haran, Abram, and calls him to leave.
entrada-biblia-03.focusQuestion: What step of trust might God be asking of you before he shows you the whole way?
entrada-biblia-03.keywordGloss: The commitment the Lord makes to Abram: from him will come a blessing for all the families of the earth.
facts: The Lord tells Abram to leave his land, his relatives, and his father's house.
The Lord promises to make Abram a great nation.
In Abram, all the families of the earth will be blessed.
Abram set out as the Lord had commanded.
Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
They set out for the land of Canaan and arrived there.

entrada-biblia-04.context: Abraham's descendants became slaves in Egypt. After the plagues, Pharaoh lets the people go, but soon changes his mind and goes after them with his army. Israel is trapped between the soldiers and the sea.
entrada-biblia-04.focusQuestion: In what situation do you need to stop fighting alone and see what the Lord will do?
entrada-biblia-04.keywordGloss: The salvation that comes from the Lord when the people have no way to save themselves.
facts: When they saw the Egyptians, the Israelites were terrified and cried out to the Lord.
The people tell Moses it would be better to serve the Egyptians.
Moses tells the people not to fear and to see the Lord's deliverance.
Moses says the Lord will fight for the people.
The Lord tells the people to move forward.
The sea would be divided so the people could cross on dry ground.

entrada-biblia-05.context: Centuries before Jesus, the prophet Isaiah speaks of a Servant of the Lord. In this passage, the people look at this wounded, humiliated Servant and try to understand why he suffers so much.
entrada-biblia-05.focusQuestion: What changes in you when you know someone carried your guilt?
entrada-biblia-05.keywordGloss: In Isaiah, the Servant of the Lord suffers for the people; the New Testament recognizes Jesus in him.
facts: The Servant was despised and rejected by people.
The Servant was pierced for our transgressions.
By his wounds the people are healed.
Everyone had gone astray like sheep.
The Lord laid on the Servant the iniquity of all.
Oppressed and humiliated, he stayed silent.

entrada-biblia-06.context: Jesus had been crucified and buried, and a large stone sealed the tomb, watched by guards. On the first day of the week, some women go there. They expect to find a body.
entrada-biblia-06.focusQuestion: What changes in your fear of death if Jesus' tomb is empty?
entrada-biblia-06.keywordGloss: Jesus comes back from death to life, as he had said, and the tomb is left empty.
facts: An angel of the Lord rolled away the stone from the entrance.
The guards trembled and became like dead men.
The angel tells the women not to be afraid.
Jesus is not in the tomb: he has risen, as he had said.
The women are sent to tell the disciples.
Jesus meets the women on the way.

entrada-biblia-07.context: Revelation is the last book of the Bible. John receives visions full of images, and much of the book shows struggle and suffering. Near the end, he sees what God is preparing to bring history to its close.
entrada-biblia-07.focusQuestion: What pain of yours will you hand over today to the God who promises to wipe away every tear?
entrada-biblia-07.keywordGloss: God remakes what the fall broke: a new heaven and a new earth, with no death or pain.
facts: John saw a new heaven and a new earth.
The holy city comes down from heaven, from God.
God will dwell with humankind, and they will be his people.
God will wipe away every tear.
Death will be no more.
The one seated on the throne makes all things new.
